issues.legal_issue: A plaint seeking division of joint-family property by metes and bounds, after status between family members has already separated, is not a suit seeking severance of joint-family status.
material_facts: The plaint referred to the separation of family branches and members, while alleging that the property had not been divided among them according to their shares.
The plaint sought accounts, determination of the property available for division, and delivery of the plaintiff’s share.
Although one sentence said the family members “were and are” joint, the court considered that sentence in the context of the plaint as a whole.
issues.conclusion: The plaint, read as a whole, sought partition of property by metes and bounds and not severance of joint-family status.
issues.legal_principle: A pleading must be interpreted by gathering its intended meaning from the whole document and its connected averments, rather than drawing an inference from an isolated expression.

rule.if: joint_family_partition_proceeding and pleading_alleges_status_separation and pleading_alleges_property_remains_undivided and pleading_seeks_division_of_shares

predicates.joint_family_partition_proceeding: The proceeding seeks division of property held by a joint family.
predicates.pleading_alleges_status_separation: The pleading states that the relevant family members or branches have already separated in status.
predicates.pleading_alleges_property_remains_undivi: The pleading states that the family property has not yet been divided among the members according to their shares.
predicates.pleading_seeks_division_of_shares: The pleading requests determination and delivery of the claimant’s share of the property.
predicates.suit_seeks_partition_by_metes_and_bounds: The suit seeks division of property by metes and bounds rather than severance of joint-family status.

issues.definition: When a joint-family property proceeding alleges both prior separation in status and undivided property, and seeks division of shares, the suit seeks partition by metes and bounds.

issues.legal_issue: An amendment correcting inadvertent wording may be allowed where the pleading already advances the intended case and the amendment does not introduce a different case.
material_facts: The plaintiff applied to delete words in the plaint that he said had been included through inadvertence and mistake.
The plaint, even without the amendment, was properly construed as seeking partition by metes and bounds rather than severance of joint-family status.
The amendment did not introduce a new case, and refusing it could require the plaintiff to bring another suit.
The court considered the amendment under Order 6, Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure and relied on L. J. Leach and Co. Ltd. v. Jardine Skinner and Co.
issues.conclusion: The amendment was properly allowed, and the suit was properly remanded for retrial.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 6, Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the court may allow an amendment where justice requires it; the rule’s purpose includes avoiding multiplicity of suits. L. J. Leach and Co. Ltd. v. Jardine Skinner and Co. establishes that the possibility that a fresh suit on an amended claim would be barred by limitation is a factor in the court’s discretion, but does not remove the power to allow an amendment when justice requires it.

rule.if: civil_suit_amendment_proceeding and proposed_change_corrects_inadvertent_wording and original_pleading_already_advances_intended_case and amendment_does_not_introduce_different_case and refusal_may_require_another_suit

predicates.civil_suit_amendment_proceeding: A party applies to amend a pleading in a civil suit.
predicates.proposed_change_corrects_inadvertent_wor: The proposed change corrects wording included through mistake or inadvertence.
predicates.original_pleading_already_advances_inten: The original pleading, properly construed, already presents the case the party intends to pursue.
predicates.amendment_does_not_introduce_different_c: The proposed change does not substitute a different case for the one already pleaded.
predicates.refusal_may_require_another_suit: Refusing the amendment may require the party to bring another suit.
predicates.amendment_may_be_allowed: The court may permit the proposed amendment.

issues.definition: If an amendment in a civil suit corrects inadvertent wording without introducing a different case, while the intended case is already pleaded and refusal may require another suit, the amendment may be allowed.
